newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end at new highs after Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end at new highs after Fed meeting.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks post sixth record close in last seven sessions * TSE also sets new intra-day high * Gold, bond markets rally after Fed meeting * 85.9 million shares traded.
Toronto's key 300 Index closed at a record high on Tuesday, propelled by a rally in gold and bond markets after the Federal Reserve kept U.S. interest rates unchanged.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 15.45 points to finish at 5299.66, eclipsing the previous record posted on September 20.
The index also set a new intra-day high of 5299.73.
But the overall market ended mixed as declining stocks outnumbered advances 471 to 428, with 323 issues flat.
Trading was brisk with volume of 85.9 million shares worth about C$1.16 billion.

The TSE's gold sector gained nearly 185 points, leading five of 14 groups higher. COMEX gold prices enjoyed a short-covering bounce after the Fed did not raise U.S. interest rates at its key policy committee meeting today.

Toronto also received a lift from Canadian bonds which outperformed U.S. treasuries. Analysts said the Fed's inaction has raised speculation that the Bank of Canada may have room to cut Canadian interest rates.
Josef Schachter, president of Schachter Asset Management, said the interest rate picture is favorable for rate sensitive stocks like banks.
"I would think the market has not finished its rally and you will see more to come," Schachter said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Among active bank stocks, Toronto-Dominion Bank closed up 0.05 at 29.05 on 1.4 million shares after earlier reaching a 52-week high of 29.40.
Royal Bank of Canada improved 0.25 to 38.35 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 38.50. BC Bancorp rose 0.01 to 0.40 after news of a merger agreement with Canadian Western Bank.
* Among gold stocks, Placer Dome Inc gained 0.95 to 33.85, while TVX Gold Inc gained 0.20 to 9.85.
